(i) a class of measures of inductive confirmation is singled out by a representation theorem, (ii) this class of measures of confirmation is uniquely coherent, and (iii) the class is the one that is most prominent in the philosophical literature.

(1) the most prominent research program of inductive logic can be represented by a unique class of ordinally equivalence classes of measures, and (2) that class of measures is the class of all probability measures on the unit interval.

The main takeaway from our work is that
a measure of partial entailment can be represented by the product of two measures, a measure of deductive entailment (a probability measure), and a measure of partial belief (a possibility measure).
the class of partial entailment measures that is singled out by our representation theorem is not only uniquely coherent, but also very natural.
